minutes.headline: Planning Board kept its Dec 22 meeting and put parking next, then signs, after the village district bylaw.
minutes.summary: The board heard an ANR land-division question, took committee and development status reports, approved the Nov 24 minutes and accepted a modification letting four utility poles stay as they are at 265 Pleasant Street. Most of the meeting was spent ranking bylaw work: village district first, then parking, with signs, solar and extending the design bylaw pushed back and an economic development committee to be proposed to the Selectmen. The regular schedule of Dec 22, Jan 12 and Jan 26 was kept.

public_comment.topic: Resident asked whether the sign bylaw covers only the village district or the whole town, and where it would be heard.
A Selectman said economic development and a possible stormwater utility fee are Selectmen goals that overlap with the board's work.

votes.motion: Formally accept the modification allowing four utility-owned poles to remain as they exist at 265 Pleasant Street.
Adjourn; next meeting December 22 at 6:30 pm.

budget_items.what_was_said: The regional commission dropped its planned move because of state cuts, is laying off staff, and faces a budget deficit to make up by June 30.
The capital planning committee recommended setting money aside to hire a consultant to study best uses of town buildings.
A per-unit payment is collected when occupancy permits are issued for the new building.
Members noted the state funding came through but should not be counted on each year.
A flat household fee in Redding's utility bylaw was cited as a model, with businesses charged on surface area.

decisions.decision: Board will sign the ANR plan the week of Dec 22 if other boards raise no problems.
Keep the regular schedule: Dec 22, Jan 12, Jan 26.
Parking design standards are the next bylaw task after the village district, then signs; solar and design bylaw extension wait until after town meeting.
Board leans toward recommending the Selectmen form an economic development committee; a draft letter to be brought in two weeks.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board ranked its bylaw work: village district first, then parking design standards, then signs, with solar and a design bylaw extension left until after town meeting.
The board moved to formally accept a modification letting four utility-owned poles stay as they are at 265 Pleasant Street; the vote was not audible in the captions.
The board leans toward recommending that the Selectmen form an economic development committee, and a draft letter is to be brought in two weeks.
The regular meeting schedule of Dec 22, Jan 12 and Jan 26 was kept.
The board said it will sign the ANR land-division plan the week of Dec 22 if other boards raise no problems.

why_it_matters: The order of bylaw work sets which zoning rules, parking and then signs, residents and businesses may be asked to vote on at a later Town Meeting.
An economic development committee and a possible stormwater utility fee, both raised as overlapping Selectmen goals, could affect future town budget costs, which are mostly taxes, and household fees.
watch_next: A draft letter to the Selectmen on an economic development committee, due in about two weeks.
Planning Board meetings on Dec 22, Jan 12 and Jan 26, including the ANR plan signing the week of Dec 22.
